newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Sterling/mark to work its way up to 2.83.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Sterling/mark to work its way up to 2.83.

text.p: Sterling/mark is set to work it's way higher and attempt to tackle peaks of 2.8331 marks where it will meet stiff resistance, chartists said.
Though dollar/mark is the primary beneficiary from mark weakness, sterling/mark looks set to ride higher on the dollar's coat tails.
"The near term outlook for sterling remains positive and we can again expect a test of the 2.8330-mark level," said Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase Investment Bank here.
"If we can break through there, that is going to extend the uptrend once again," he added.
And if sterling/mark can climb above 2.8330, chartists expected a move up to the top of the recent up channel, targeting 2.8530.
Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America, said the pound's break above 2.80 marks had opened up a triangle of targets up to around 2.90.
But he and others expected the uptrend to be muted and said sterling would struggle to break 2.8330. Though a downside move was unlikely, abundant support was at hand.
"If there is a break below 2.8150, where there is chart support, we're looking at 2.8045, yesterday's low," said Dunne.
"That is the key support to watch now," he added.
Below those levels, chartists said there was medium term support at 2.8085 marks and 2.8075. These must be held to sustain the uptrend, they said.
Chartists expected little drama from cable, as it again looked set to remain in a tight range between $1.63 and $1.6360.
"If anything, sterling/mark might lag dollar/mark a little bit and that will keep cable flat to softer," said Dunne.
Support was evident at $1.6240, the previous low, and then at $1.6235, the low set on Wednesday.
But if sterling could break through resistance at $1.6345, chartists said $1.6380 would be challenged.
